title: pause everything from somewhere else, and play back exactly that set
asserts: a core that advertises `globalPause` lets a client that is not the desktop sleep every live agent at once and bring back exactly that set. `pauseAll` answers with a `pauseState` naming the sessions it slept - no reply of its own, the same shape `sleepSession` has, because the set IS the answer - and each of them then exits, so the RAM the pause was taken for actually comes back. What the set does NOT contain is the load-bearing half: a session that exited on its own before the pause is not in it and is not woken by the play, which is the same refusal `sleepSession` makes for a session with no live pty and for the same reason - a crashed row resurrected by a global play is indistinguishable from one somebody paused, and reviving it is the bug this whole ticket is about. A session already asleep when the pause lands is excluded by the identical rule (`targets` filters on liveness, not on the dormant flag), so it stays the user's own sleep rather than becoming this pause's to wake. `resumeAll` clears the set before it revives anything, so the state a client renders its button off stops saying "paused" the moment the play starts and a revival that fails leaves a clickable sleeping row rather than a pause that never lifts.

steps.note: two sessions, because everything this frame promises is about which of them the set contains
this one ends before the pause is taken, which is the row a play must never resurrect

the set, and what is missing from it - published BEFORE any pty dies, so a client is never told about a kill it has no record of a pause for. The live agent is in; the one that ended on its own is not, because a play driven off anything broader would wake it as if somebody had paused it
and the CLI tree is actually freed - a pause that left the process running would not give back the ~300MB it is taken for
cleared before a single pty respawns: the button must read "paused" for exactly as long as the pause is in effect
a play is real `--resume` processes spread over bounded lanes, not a flag flip; this outlasts one spawn
exactly the session the pause took is awake again, and its dormant flag is cleared - waking is `reactivate` under the hood, which clears it on every path that respawns a pty
and the one that was never in the set is still dead. "Exactly that set" is only a promise if this row stays down
an attach to a row with no pty replays its exit; consumed here so the cleanup below cannot mistake it for the woken session's

this scenario's own cleanup, and one more assertion in disguise: the kill only produces an exit if the client is subscribed to the pty the PLAY spawned. A revive makes a new session object under the old id, so a subscription keyed on the id alone still points at the dead one - which is silence where a client is waiting for output and for this exit
